references.text: The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus returns across the sea and the crowd welcomes him on the shore.
The parallel passage in Matthew where a synagogue leader comes to Jesus after he has returned, introducing the same account of Jairus.
The preceding context where Jesus was asked to leave the region of the Gerasenes, and the healed man wanted to follow him – now Jesus returns across the sea.
Here too the crowds welcome Jesus (ἀπεδέξατο / ἀπεδέξαντο), showing a recurring pattern in Luke where the masses eagerly wait for and receive Jesus.
The crowd gathered again around Jesus by the sea, illustrating the repeated pattern of large crowds waiting for him and seeking him out.

The crowds were looking for Jesus and tried to keep him from leaving, which illustrates the strong expectation people had toward Jesus – the same motif as in Luke 8:40 where everyone was waiting for him.
